analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1678-2113); the file is documentation only. The patch excerpt shows the head change as a new v0.10.4 candidate section replacing the v0.10.3 heading at lines 11-13, plus about 160 new lines. The excerpt is truncated, so I could not review the rest of the added section text. No executable code, configuration, wire contract or threat-model definitions are modified in the visible evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

From the visible head excerpt, the rollout notes describe a cache-receipt mismatch (`prompt_anchor_mismatch`) when provider and coordinator prompt rendering disagree. The stated effect is a quarantine of cache affinity for up to 10 minutes, with requests still served. That relates to the T-041 and SEC-035 cache-routing surface, but the note describes an availability or efficiency effect, not new disclosure. The notes also describe grammar-constrained JSON for Qwen, which ends in a 422 on truncation, and forced `tool_choice` advertisement. These are provider behavior changes in other files not supplied here.

The base text I examined covers cache-read pricing, the SSD cache write budget (150 to 750 GB/day), artifact revision integrity and App Attest history. It only provides historical context and is unchanged by this PR. The 750 GB/day write-budget raise predates this PR and appears in the base, so I did not treat it as new.

Remaining question for the next pass: the source files implementing the v0.10.4 claims (Qwen JSON grammar, tool_constraint_models, prompt sidecar planning) are not in this batch. Their security behavior, including cache scope isolation and TTFT oracle effects, is unverified from the changelog alone.
